title: Tokyo dark on the US 2-Year auction day itself — the in-between-holidays day created by Rule 3(3) of Japan's Act on National Holidays
source: EST: jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/index.html (Market Holidays, the page's own 'Update : Feb. 06, 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes) — the 2026 panel reads verbatim 'Sep. 22 (Tue.) Holiday 2', and the page's footnote 2 reads verbatim 'September 22, 2026, is a holiday in accordance with Rule 3, Paragraph 3 of Act on National Holidays', i.e. the statutory rule that turns a single weekday sandwiched between two national holidays into a holiday itself (09-21 Respect for the Aged Day, 09-23 Autumnal Equinox). The same page's standing rule is 'JPX markets are closed on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and on the dates indicated below.' Corroborated at a second, independent primary in the same session: Japan's Cabinet Office national-holiday file www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv (HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS), whose 2026 rows read 2026/9/21 敬老の日, 2026/9/22 休日 (literally 'holiday', the Cabinet Office's own label for exactly this in-between case), 2026/9/23 秋分の日. Stays estimate on the two standing counts the sibling jpx-market-closure entries already record, neither of them date doubt: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED during the treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22 adjacency sweep (2026-09-15, D-7) — this is the only corridor entry that falls on the proposing event's own date. Counting weekends, JPX is shut for FIVE consecutive sessions, Sat 2026-09-19 through Wed 2026-09-23: the longest single blackout run in Japan's 2026 calendar, and the 1:00pm ET 2-Year note auction prices inside it. WHY IT IS FILED AND WHAT IT EXPLICITLY DOES NOT LICENSE. The obvious hunch — Tokyo dark thins the Japanese bid, so indirect share should print soft, which would fire the proposing event's own FT-47 (indirect below 57.2%) for a mechanical rather than an economic reason — was MEASURED and is a null. Across 1,108 Treasury note/bond auctions since 2016 (Fiscal Data auctions_query, shares computed over competitive accepted, pulled direct 2026-09-15), the 37 held on a Japanese national holiday drew mean indirect 63.35% vs 61.89% on Tokyo-open days: the WRONG SIGN for the hunch, Welch t=+0.850. Dealer takedown 20.87% vs 23.52%, t=-1.412, also the wrong sign for any forced-absorption story. On 2-Year notes alone (n=171) it is nearly exact: dark 55.22% (n=9) vs open 55.44% (n=162), Welch t=-0.050. Inside blackouts of three or more consecutive dark sessions (n=15 auctions) mean indirect is 60.57% vs 61.89%, and that subsample contains both tails (2018-09-24 at 40.0%, 2025-02-24 at 85.5%). The nearest precedent is exact: the 2025-09-23 2-Year auction was itself held on Autumnal Equinox Day and printed indirect 57.7% / dealer 11.5%, both on that series' own norm. So the entry's job is to make the blackout VISIBLE and pre-empt a post-hoc excuse — a weak 09-22 indirect print may NOT be discounted as a Tokyo-holiday artifact, because the base rate says it is not one. Impact low: no Japan-listed symbol is tracked here and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or Tokyo-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
